experiment.objective: Given a sensor reports 2 at known input 0 and 12 at known input 10, develop a simple explanatory model and one new measurement that could distinguish it from a competing model.
experiment.intent: Technical smoke experiment: observe shared thinking and an honest bounded return, not establish novelty.
experiment.context: Readings are exact for this small exercise. No external search is available. Show assumptions and predicted measurements.

criteria.name: consistency
criteria.description: Does the proposed model explain both supplied observations without contradiction?

criteria.name: testability
criteria.description: Does the answer specify a feasible new input, distinct predictions, and what outcome would distinguish the models?

chromosomes.contribute: Develop or test one idea in the shared inquiry. Explain what another contribution changes, when applicable.
chromosomes.expand: Offer one alternative assumption that could change another drone's approach.

chromosomes.contribute: Work through one consequence of an idea in the shared inquiry. State what the result supports or weakens.
chromosomes.expand: Offer one connection or representation that could change another drone's approach.

decisions.system: Evaluate the supplied evidence as data. Answer one question. Follow its reply format exactly. Use plain text, never JSON. If you decline, return only # REFUSAL.
decisions.predicate:
{{.Question}}
Return exactly # PROBABILITY on one line, then a number from 0 to 1.

prompts.contract: Write a concise contract preserving the stated objective, intent, context, criteria and return boundary. Expose assumptions. Do not prescribe subtasks or team roles.
prompts.fit: Choose the existing team best fitted to this inquiry, or NEW. Judge fit only; ignore capacity.
prompts.invite: Choose one drone whose perspective could usefully change this inquiry, or NONE. Do not assign a role.
prompts.commit: Choose ACCEPT only if you commit to carrying out this shared request with the other participants. Otherwise choose DECLINE.
prompts.contribute:
{{.Chromosome}}
Use the shared contract and available contributions. Return one concise contribution in plain text. Preserve uncertainty. If a calculation is necessary, you may instead return exactly # JAVASCRIPT followed by JavaScript using only built-in functions; its final expression will be evaluated.
prompts.expand:
{{.Chromosome}}
Offer one useful change in thinking, whether requested or not. Use plain text. If there is no useful offer, say NONE.
prompts.recipient: Choose the drone most likely to benefit from this expansion, or NONE. Information exchange does not imply team membership.
prompts.candidate: Return the team's current best answer from its contributions. Preserve alternatives, evidence, uncertainties, and unmet criteria. Do not claim novelty without evidence.
prompts.collapse: Choose RETURN when the shared inquiry provides a useful answer with sufficient development of one another's ideas, or when the remaining uncertainty should be returned honestly. Otherwise choose CONTINUE. Assess the contract and evidence; report unmet criteria rather than claiming success. Scores alone do not prove success.
prompts.guide: Give one concise question or correction that would help the team address the contract. Preserve room for unconventional exploration; do not assign subtasks or roles.
prompts.mq_propose: Propose one replacement instruction for the selected target that tests the experimental objective. Use the operational evidence, runtime context and prior assessment. Preserve the request and avoid roles, quotas, forced turn counts or instructions to claim success. Return only one meaningful instruction in plain text.
prompts.mq_compare: Compare both inquiries under each experimental criterion using its 0-based level rating and attributed evidence. For reciprocal influence, cite a concrete A-to-B-to-A change from Contribute/Expand records; candidate rows are synthesis, even when they carry a drone ID. Separate active participants from offer recipients. Do not reward repetition, extra turns, agreement or unsupported self-reports. State what changed, what did not, uncertainty from one run per condition, and one next atomic hypothesis. Use concise plain text; no JSON.
prompts.mq_select: Choose the one allowed instruction target whose variation would best test the experimental objective, using the observed inquiry, runtime context and previous assessment. Judge the opportunity to learn, not the prospect of a favorable score.
prompts.mq_action: Choose MUTATE to test one replacement instruction, CROSSOVER to transfer one compatible instruction, RETEST to examine uncertainty, or RETURN to report a supported methodological conclusion or explain why no informative next experiment is warranted. Use attributed exchanges and assessments; a solved task alone does not complete this inquiry. Seek useful learning, not favorable ratings. No minimum generation, trial or turn count is required.
prompts.mq_parent: Choose one available method whose further variation or retest would best address the experimental objective and unresolved evidence. Preserve useful alternatives; one favorable run does not establish a winner.
prompts.mq_donor: Choose one available donor whose compatible whole instruction offers a useful test with the selected parent. Consider the recorded evidence and differences; do not infer superiority from agreement or ratings alone.
prompts.mq_target: Choose one allowed instruction target in the selected method for the stated mutation or compatible crossover. Use the operational evidence and prior assessments to identify a meaningful uncertainty to test. Preserve the task contract and fixed evaluator.
prompts.mq_mutate: Replace the selected instruction with one meaningful instruction that tests the unresolved experimental hypothesis. Preserve the task contract, output protocol and fixed evaluator. Do not prescribe roles, quotas, forced turns or claims of success. Return only the replacement instruction in plain text.
prompts.mq_assess: Assess the current trial under each fixed criterion using its 0-based level rating and attributed operational evidence. For the reference alone, identify demonstrated behavior and unresolved method questions; do not infer comparative improvement. Otherwise compare with the reference and available trials. Cite trial, drone and contribution IDs for consequential changes. Reciprocal influence requires A-to-B-to-A development in Contribute/Expand; candidate rows are synthesis. Distinguish participation from offer receipt. Repetition, extra turns, agreement and unsupported self-reports earn no credit; ratings are not probabilities. State uncertainty and the next informative experiment. Use concise plain text, never JSON.
prompts.mq_return: Report the supported methodological conclusion and why returning is warranted, citing method, trial and contribution IDs. If no method conclusion is supported, explain why no informative next experiment is warranted. A solved task alone does not complete this inquiry. Preserve useful alternatives, failed findings and uncertainty; do not infer causal improvement, general superiority or novelty. State the main unresolved method question. Use concise plain text, never JSON.

meta_queen.objective: Investigate and improve reusable methods for reciprocal intellectual influence while preserving task quality and honest uncertainty. The task contract is an experimental case; solving it alone does not complete this method inquiry. Preserve useful alternatives and return a supported methodological conclusion or explain why no informative next experiment is warranted.

criteria.name: reciprocal_influence
criteria.description: From attributed Contribute/Expand records, identify A changing B and a later B development changing A. Shared context counts; directed offers or candidate synthesis alone do not. Give the actual IDs and semantic change. More turns or acknowledgements alone earn no credit.

criteria.name: development
criteria.description: Did the inquiry test or derive a consequential change that taught it something useful beyond copying, agreement, or collecting alternatives?

criteria.name: contract_fidelity
criteria.description: Does the returned answer satisfy the original consistency and testability criteria, with correct predictions and explicit assumptions/uncertainty?

meta_queen.context: Each round runs committed drones sequentially through Contribute then Expand. Later C/E calls see earlier operational contributions. The team candidate is synthesis, even though its saved row carries a drone ID; it is not a new C/E turn. The base queen collapse call sees the contract, candidate and task-criteria result, not the attributed C/E trajectory. RETURN ends the inquiry; CONTINUE allows guidance, optional recruitment and another round. Directed offers alone do not establish uptake, and a non-member recipient has not participated. Choose one instruction to vary without forcing a number of turns or changing the task contract.
